title: Toposort a tiny DAG
starter:
(* A tiny DAG, given as a list of nodes. Every name appears once. *)
type node = { name : string; srcs : string list }

(* Return the names reachable from root, each exactly once, in depth-first
   post-order: visit a node's srcs left to right first, then the node itself.
   Every node comes after all of its sources. *)
let topo (graph : node list) (root : string) : string list =
  [ root ]
hints: This is the same 'visit sources first, then the node' walk as the toposort stepper above. Recursion fits it naturally.
Write a recursive `go name`: if `name` hasn't been seen, mark it seen, call `go` on each of its `srcs` left to right, then record `name`.

Keep a seen set (a `Hashtbl` works well) and skip names already in it. In a DAG it doesn't matter whether you mark a node on entry or when you emit it; entry marking only matters for graphs with cycles. If you build the result by consing onto a list, reverse it at the end.

answer.explain: The solution does a depth-first post-order walk: each node is marked in a `Hashtbl` on first visit, its sources are walked left to right, and only then is it added to the output. The seen table makes shared subgraphs cost one visit, which is why the 31-level doubling DAG finishes instantly instead of taking 2^31 steps.
